title: Retention and telemetry SLA phrasing for enterprise legal
content:
Purpose and audience:
This note is a short, pragmatic playbook for GTM and legal-facing conversations about telemetry and audit-log commitments. Primary audience: AE/SEs, solutions engineers, deal/legal reviewers, and CISO buyers. Use it to (1) answer RFP/SECURITY questionnaire items, (2) propose contract language redlines, and (3) align on default vs enterprise/contracted behaviors.

Key principles we want represented in customer-facing language:
- Predictable retention: provide clear, quantifiable retention windows by data class (structured audit events, request traces, raw payloads, telemetry metrics).
- Exportability & portability: customers can request exports in machine-readable formats within a bounded SLA.
- Minimization & redaction: we default to removing high-risk PII from telemetry and offer configurable redaction for enterprise tiers.
- Isolation options: hosted defaults vs dedicated/private deployments have different storage/retention commitments and controls (KMS, VPC).
- Contracted flexibility: retention windows and export SLAs are negotiable for enterprise deals; include clear fallback/default language.

Suggested default table (language to copy into FAQs/RFP responses):
- Structured audit events (authn, authz, API request metadata): retained 365 days for Enterprise; 90 days for Standard plans. Exportable as JSON/CSV in 7 business days on request.
- Token-level request traces / raw request payloads (full prompt + response): retained 30 days by default; can be disabled or shortened on request. For HIPAA-sensitive customers, default is disabled unless explicitly enabled and covered by BAAs.
- Aggregated telemetry and metrics (latency, error rates, model throughput): retained 540 days for trend analysis; can be reduced for customers that prefer shorter retention.
- Model evaluation traces and prompts used for quality monitoring: retained 90 days; customers can opt-out of use for model improvement in Enterprise agreements.

Guidance for evidence/controls we can cite in RFPs and buyer briefings:
- Encryption: data at rest encrypted with AES-256; keys managed in our KMS. Customer-managed keys (CMK) available for Dedicated/Private plans (note: requires additional contractual terms).
- Access controls: audit logs include discrete events for read/export actions, with role-based access enforced in the Console and via APIs.
- Tamper-evidence: logs stored with immutable write-once append semantics in the telemetry pipeline for a default 180-day WORM interval for audit evidence.
- Redaction: PII redaction pipeline available; recommended for healthcare customers as default on hosted platforms if enabled.

Example concise contract clauses (sales-friendly):
- "Audit Log Retention: Redwood Inference will retain structured audit log events for the service for a period of 365 days (the ‘Retention Period’). Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide an export of Customer's audit logs in JSON/CSV format within seven (7) business days. Customer may request shorter retention periods for their account subject to mutual agreement"
- "Sensitive Payloads: By default, recorded raw request payloads (including unredacted prompts/responses) are retained for up to thirty (30) days and are used for debugging and service quality. For customers subject to HIPAA or other regulatory constraints, raw payload recording can be disabled or limited via contract or feature configuration; in such cases Redwood will rely on Customer-provided monitoring hooks and will not retain raw payloads beyond operational troubleshooting windows unless otherwise agreed."
- "Key Management: For Dedicated and Private deployments, Customer may elect to use Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) for encryption of audit logs and stored telemetry. Use of CMKs is subject to enrollment and acceptance criteria outlined in the Redwood Key Management Addendum."

What to avoid in customer-facing language (common pitfalls to redact):
- Ambiguous words like "indefinitely" or "as needed" without metricized SLAs.
- Overpromising export formats or timelines that require engineering work.
- Saying "we never see customer data" without qualifying telemetry that is necessarily processed by the control plane in hosted tiers.

Escalation and redlines playbook for Legal/AE when customer pushes back:
- If customer demands <90-day retention for structured audit logs: propose a middle ground of 180 days with additional contractual audit rights.
- If customer requires deletion of existing telemetry immediately on execution: escalate to Security + Product to confirm feasibility; propose a 30-day deletion SLA for structured logs and 60-day for archived telemetry while retention removal workflows run.
- If customer requires BAAs or stricter HIPAA language: route to partnerships/legal immediately; hosted defaults must be validated for the design with the Privacy/Compliance team before signature.

Competitive notes (quick signal map for AEs):
- Major managed-LLM API providers: often keep raw traces 30–90 days; limited exportability for standard plans; CMK for enterprise.
- Traditional cloud vendors: retention for audit logs often 365+ days but require additional storage charges; some vendors have built-in WORM and immutability options as add-ons.
- Open-source self-hosted solutions: offer maximal control for retention but lack turnkey export/forensics playbooks and require customer ops to implement secure key management.

Suggested rebut templates for objection handling:
- Objection: "We can't have raw requests stored."
  - Rebuttal: "We can disable raw-request retention for your account and provide structured audit events only; for HIPAA customers we default to disabling raw payload storage unless explicitly enabled under a BAA."
- Objection: "We need exports faster than 7 days."
  - Rebuttal: "We can add an accelerated export SLA (e.g., 48–72 hours) as a negotiated term for enterprise commitments; typical implementation requires scheduled data-pull and is billable as an operational service."

Operational notes for SRE/Product when asked by Legal/Procurement:
- Export complexity: real-time exports are feasible for structured events but expensive for raw traces — recommend contract language that limits scope to structured events unless customer pays for raw trace export.
- Deletion propagation: deletion of backups/archives may take additional time; use a 30–60 day window in contract language and communicate this clearly in data subject requests (DSR) playbooks.
- Audit copies: maintain internal retention of telemetry for investigation but mark data as inaccessible to product/engineering after a legal/contractual deletion event; implement a documented gating process for emergency access with approvals.

One-pager for AE quick-sell (copy/paste friendly):
- "Redwood provides tiered, predictable telemetry and audit-log retention: default structured audit events retained 365 days (enterprise), raw request traces 30 days (can be disabled), and metrics retained up to 540 days for capacity planning. Exports available on request; CMK support for Dedicated/Private deployments; HIPAA configurations available under a BAA."

Open questions and product asks (for roadmap coordination):
- Engineering: provide UI to configure retention per data class at the org level (0/30/90/365/540) and generate export bundles with retention metadata.
- Product: define standard enterprise SKUs that include accelerated export (72h) and extended retention for compliance (up to 7 years) with pricing.
- Security/Privacy: codify the minimum redaction heuristics we apply to telemetry by default and publish sample sanitized events for customer review.

Action items / next steps:
- Share with Legal for templating into the Master Services Agreement and Data Processing Addendum (Ethan).
- Build a short FAQ and one-pager for AEs and SEs for pitch decks and security questionnaires (María).
- Open a small infra GH issue to scope export SLA automation and retention config UI (JIRA: INFRA-921).
- Sync with Product to prioritize retention config in the next quarterly roadmap (owner: Sofia).

Appendix: Example RFP answers (short)
Q: "How long do you retain audit logs?"
A: "By default we retain structured audit logs 365 days on enterprise plans and 90 days on standard plans; retention is configurable by contract for enterprise customers."

Q: "Can we restrict or disable raw request storage?"
A: "Yes — raw request recording can be disabled on a per-account basis and is the recommended default for HIPAA-covered use cases. When disabled, structured audit events remain available for operational and security needs."

Q: "How quickly can we get a copy of our logs?"
A: "Structured audit logs are exportable in JSON/CSV and delivered within seven business days by default; accelerated delivery is available as a negotiated enterprise term."

---
Notes: keep this doc lean. We'll iterate once Legal and Security drop redlines. Use this as our canonical GTM phrasing when answering procurement/security from enterprise buyers.
